00_liability_model.name: 00_liability_model
00_liability_model.text:
## 00 Liability model

- [MUST P-LIAB-1] Law decides what a vendor owes the customer, and no vendor contract or TripDesk policy can take a legal right away: an entitlement compute_entitlement gives is owed even where the vendor's fare_rules say less.
- [MUST P-LIAB-2] The vendor contract fills what law leaves open and decides vendor-side refunds, changes and charges: flight_cancel, flight_change, rail_cancel and ride_cancel_scheduled apply the vendor's fare_rules, and hotel_cancel the property policy the reservation carries.
- [MUST P-LIAB-3] TripDesk policy governs only TripDesk's own actions and money, and TripDesk never grants a vendor-side refund the vendor has not granted.
- [SHOULD P-LIAB-4] When two layers disagree, the agent should follow the layer that owns the question and record the conflict with add_note.

10_law_and.name: 10_law_and
10_law_and.text:
## 10 Law and regulation

- [MUST P-DOT-REFUND] [V2] On a flight within, to or from the US (region US, or INTL for an international flight to or from the US), if an airline cancels a flight or makes a significant change (3 hours or more domestic, 6 hours or more international) and the passenger does not accept the alternative, the passenger is owed a cash refund including taxes and ancillary fees: issue_refund pays the refundable amount quote_cancellation gives for the platform_booking_id (the booking's total, taxes and ancillary fees included, less only a fee P-DOT-AGENT-FEE lets the ticket agent keep).
- [MUST P-DOT-24H] [V2] The 24-hour cancellation rule binds airlines only and never a ticket agent such as TripDesk, so on a booking whose payment has merchant_of_record platform it never makes issue_refund pay cash for a value flight_cancel returns as a credit.
- [MUST P-DOT-AGENT] [V1] A ticket agent that is merchant of record refunds the customer: where the booking's payment has merchant_of_record platform, issue_refund pays the refund to that payment_id, to a card within 7 business days of the airline's eligibility notice, other payments within 20 calendar days.
- [MUST P-DOT-AGENT-FEE] [V1] On a US booking, the refundable amount quote_cancellation gives keeps back the ticket agent's own fee only if the fee is per passenger and was disclosed as non-refundable at purchase.
- [MUST P-DOT-CASH] [V1] Where the DOT rule gives a cash refund, a vendor's own figure for the refund time, a credit at the vendor's discretion or a shorter credit validity never replaces the DOT figure: issue_refund pays it in cash whatever refund_form the vendor's fare_rules give, to wallet credit only as IP-14 allows.
- [SHOULD P-DOT-NODELAY] [V2] No US federal rule requires cash compensation for a delay, or for a missed connection caused by a separate booking.
- [MUST P-EU261] [V1] EU261 covers flights only, never trains: flights departing from an EU airport on any carrier, and flights arriving into the EU on an EU carrier. For a cancellation or denied boarding the operating carrier owes 250 EUR for flights of 1500 km or less, 400 EUR for intra-EU flights over 1500 km and other flights of 1500 to 3500 km, and 600 EUR for all other flights, unless the cause of a cancellation was extraordinary; boarding denied against the passenger's will is always compensated. The figure is per passenger, in EUR, set by the flight's distance and never by the booking's total or any vendor booking amount: compute_entitlement gives it times the booking's pax. The 2004 text of EU261 governs every case before 2027-10-23 (formerly P-EU261-TEXT).
- [MUST P-EU261-NOTICE] [V1] No compensation is owed for a cancellation notified at least 14 days before departure, or 7 to 14 days before with re-routing departing at most 2 hours earlier and arriving less than 4 hours later, or under 7 days before with re-routing departing at most 1 hour earlier and arriving less than 2 hours later.
- [SHOULD P-EU261-REDUCE] [V1] The carrier may halve the compensation when the re-routing it offered arrives within 2, 3 or 4 hours of the original arrival for the 250, 400 and 600 EUR bands.
- [MUST P-EU261-CASELAW] [V2] TripDesk applies CJEU case law (Sturgeon, C-402/07 and C-432/07): an arrival delay of 3 hours or more is compensated as a cancellation, unless the cause was extraordinary.
- [MUST P-EU-RAIL] [V1] An EU rail passenger is owed 25 percent of the ticket price (the booking's total) for a delay of 60 to 119 minutes and 50 percent from 120 minutes, paid within one month of the claim; the carrier may set a minimum payout of at most 4 EUR per ticket, and nothing is owed if the passenger was told of the delay before buying or the delay came from extraordinary circumstances outside the railway, the passenger's own fault or a third party.
- [MUST P-DB] [V1] Deutsche Bahn pays no delay compensation under 4 EUR (the min_payout in its fare_rules), and a claim expires 1 year (365 days, the claim_window_days in its fare_rules) after the ticket's validity ends.
- [MUST P-IR] [V1] A full Indian Railways refund for a train more than 3 hours (180 minutes, the tdr_late_min in its fare_rules) late is due only if the TDR is filed before the train's actual departure.
- [SHOULD P-HOTEL-LAW] No statute here gives a refund when a hotel cancels; vendor contract and TripDesk policy govern that case.

20_vendor_contracts.name: 20_vendor_contracts
20_vendor_contracts.text:
## 20 Vendor contracts and fare rules

- [MUST P-DELTA] [V1] Delta Classic and Extra tickets from the US or Canada have no change fee, any fare difference applies, and a ticket not changed or cancelled before departure has no remaining value.
- [MUST P-DELTA-CANCEL] [V1] A voluntary cancellation of a Delta Basic or Classic ticket after the 24-hour window returns the remaining value minus the fare's cancellation charge (99 to 500 USD Basic, 0 to 400 USD Classic) as an eCredit, never as cash.
- [MUST P-DELTA-BASIC] [V2] Delta Basic Economy tickets cannot be changed.
- [MUST P-AMTRAK-FARE] [V1] Amtrak Value fares forfeit 30 percent of the fare when cancelled before departure, Flex fares are fully refundable, and a no-show or a ticket not cancelled before departure forfeits the whole fare.
- [MUST P-AMTRAK-DISRUPT] [V1] Amtrak publishes no cash delay compensation, so no delay entitlement exists for an Amtrak train.
- [MUST P-LYFT-CANCEL] [V2] A scheduled Lyft ride carries a cancellation fee only if cancelled within 1 hour of pickup, whether or not a driver was matched; the fee amount is [synthetic].
- [MUST P-HILTON] [V1] Hotel cancellation terms are per property, each reservation carries its property policy, and a late cancellation fee per that policy is taken once: kept from the prepaid amount (quote_cancellation gives it as the vendor penalty, IP-15), and hotel_cancel charges only the part the prepaid amount not yet refunded does not cover.
- [SHOULD P-HILTON-HOLD] [synthetic] A guaranteed reservation is held for late arrival as its property policy says, and the agent should tell the property of a late arrival with hotel_add_note. A property is told of a late arrival by hotel_add_note on the reservation or by vendor_send with request_type late_arrival on its booking, where the property accepts that type; either write counts as telling it.
- [MUST SC-LAKESIDE-1] [synthetic] A Lakeside Inn cancellation of a confirmed booking whose cancel_event has customer_confirmed false is a supplier fault, and reclassify_cancellation records it with cause supplier_fault.
- [MUST SC-LAKESIDE-2] [synthetic] On supplier fault Lakeside Inn owes TripDesk the customer's relocation cost difference; a vendor_send with request_type relocation_claim claims it within 90 days (the claim_window_days in the vendor's fare_rules) after the last night.
- [MUST SC-RIVERNORTH] [synthetic] River North Hotel bookings cancel free until 7 days before arrival (15:00 local time on the check-in day less 7 days, the cancel_free_until every River North property_policy carries), and a later cancellation or a no-show keeps the late_cancel_fee_amount of that policy (P-HILTON).

Background (SC-LAKESIDE-3, synthetic): a rate-display dispute between TripDesk and the property is a matter between them
and never changes what the customer is owed.

30_tripdesk_internal.name: 30_tripdesk_internal
30_tripdesk_internal.text:
## 30 TripDesk internal policy (IP-TRIPDESK-v3) [synthetic]

Background (IP-0): every case arrives as one written message, the agent cannot ask the customer anything, and where
something cannot be resolved safely the agent takes the safe fallback (escalate, decline or do nothing).

- [MUST IP-1] Before reading or changing any customer data, the agent verifies the requester with verify_identity (email on file, one booking id, last 4 digits of the card that paid for it), and every write it then makes is on a booking of the customer verify_identity verified.
- [MUST IP-1b] If verification fails, the agent changes nothing: every write other than verify_identity needs the customer's row in sessions, which verify_identity writes only on success.
- [MUST IP-2] The agent charges the customer, or makes an irreversible change, only where the message explicitly authorizes that action and amount.
- [MUST IP-3] When a loss is a supplier fault and a cost is at stake for TripDesk (money TripDesk paid or owes the customer for the supplier's failure) that no vendor promise covers, the agent records it with reclassify_cancellation and files a claim for that cost with the supplier through vendor_send; a promise a vendor's staff made is escalated per IP-9c instead, and a supplier fault with no TripDesk cost needs no claim under this sentence (a sentence that names its own claim, such as CR-CAR-NOCAR or SC-LAKESIDE-2, still applies). The cost IP-3 covers is money TripDesk bears that the vendor's refund of its own booking does not return, such as a replacement or relocation cost the supplier's failure caused or a chargeback accepted for a vendor's fault (CB-RECOVER); the refund issue_refund or issue_refund_legacy pays back on a booking the vendor itself cancelled or failed to provide (P-DOT-REFUND, CR-FMC-REFUND, CR-CAR-NOCAR, CV-REASON) is no such cost, since the vendor's refund of its cancellation settles it, so that refund is not claimed from the supplier under this sentence, and is recorded with reclassify_cancellation only where another sentence says so (such as SC-LAKESIDE-1).
- [MUST IP-3b] The agent never tells the customer what the supplier said unless the supplier agreed.
- [MUST IP-5] Where law gives a cash refund right, the agent discloses it before offering any credit.
- [MUST IP-6] The agent never makes a refund the customer is owed depend on dropping a dispute, signing a waiver or writing a review.
- [MUST IP-7] Escalation queues are tier2_goodwill (Goodwill desk, 48 h), supplier_relations (72 h), legal (24 h) and safety (4 h).
- [MUST IP-7b] The agent escalates on legal threats, safety issues, suspected fraud, or amounts above its authority.
- [SHOULD IP-7c] The agent should give the customer the escalation id, owner and SLA.
- [MUST IP-7d] An escalation to the legal or safety queue carries no amount: the agent leaves amount at 0 or omits it, because those queues review a matter and pay nothing; only an escalation under IP-9, IP-9c or CARE-EXTRAORDINARY carries an amount, the one IP-9d or that sentence gives.
- [MUST IP-8] The agent never promises discretionary vendor compensation or says a vendor agreed when it has not.
- [MUST IP-9] An open commitment from get_commitments is escalated with escalate to tier2_goodwill with its commitment_id, on the platform_booking_id the commitment names, for the amount IP-9d gives, and the agent never pays that amount with a refund; other refunds on the booking follow their own rules, and a vendor promise on the same booking is escalated separately per IP-9c.
- [MUST IP-9d] The amount of an IP-9 or IP-9c escalation is the cost the customer bore for the promised item, capped by the figure the promise names (a commitment's max_amount, or an amount in the contact row's text): the promised item is what the promise says TripDesk or the vendor will pay, refund or cover; that cost is the total of the documents get_documents gives for the item, or with none the total of the TripDesk bookings that bought it, less what was already refunded on them, and for a promise to cover the difference between a replacement and the booking it replaced it is the replacement's total less the replaced booking's total (a refund of the replaced booking does not lower it); with no such cost on file it is the figure the promise names. An escalation of an open commitment always carries an amount above zero and never above its max_amount, and the agent never pays a promised item with issue_refund or issue_refund_legacy: not on the booking the commitment names (IP-9), and not on a replacement the customer booked for it, which is a booking of the same product type made at or after the commitment's created_at.
- [MUST IP-9b] A superseded commitment does not apply.
- [MUST IP-9e] The agent escalates to tier2_goodwill only an open commitment under IP-9, with its commitment_id; a cost no open commitment covers is never escalated to tier2_goodwill: not a hotel the customer bought after a flight was cancelled (weather included), not a loss TripDesk recovers from the supplier (CB-RECOVER, IP-3), and not a fee, fare or refund the customer is owed under another rule.
- [MUST IP-9c] A contact history row in which an actor other than the agent, a supervisor or the customer (a brand or vendor desk, or a vendor's staff) promises that the vendor will pay, refund or cover a cost, or review it for payment, is a vendor liability: the agent escalates it with escalate to supplier_relations on the platform_booking_id the row names, for the amount IP-9d gives, and never pays that amount with a refund; a row that only informs or refuses promises nothing, a later refusal does not cancel an earlier promise, and other refunds on the booking follow their own rules.
- [MUST IP-14] A refund goes to the original payment, and to wallet credit only where the customer's message asks for wallet credit; where law gives a cash refund right (P-DOT-REFUND, P-DOT-CASH) the agent pays wallet credit only after it disclosed that right (IP-5) and the message still asks for credit, and a booking marked legacy_system is refunded only through issue_refund_legacy, which pays wallet credit (IP-17).
- [MUST IP-15] Before issue_refund or issue_refund_legacy pays back a cancelled, disrupted or unused booking, the agent calls quote_cancellation for the booking (a refund of a ride charge the vendor approved in a fare_review is that approved amount and needs no quote, CV-RIDE-FARE), and the refund never exceeds the refundable amount it gives: the amount paid less the vendor penalty, the platform fee kept and the refunds already requested or paid.
- [MUST IP-16] TripDesk refunds only bookings where it is merchant of record; where the vendor is merchant of record, the vendor refunds.
- [MUST IP-17] issue_refund_legacy is used only for bookings marked legacy_system.
- [MUST IP-18] Outside the US, the refundable amount quote_cancellation gives keeps back TripDesk's own fee only if the fee is per passenger and was disclosed as non-refundable at purchase.
- [MUST IP-11] When a status_events row gives the projected arrival of an inbound flight or train, the agent rebooks the earliest flight that departs at least 90 minutes after the later of that arrival and a ready time the customer's message states (times compared with their offsets), and changes it before the booked flight departs; a train counts from its arrival at its station, the same 90 minutes for a station at the airport and for one in the city.
- [MUST IP-12] When the customer already has a scheduled ride that the new ride replaces, the agent cancels that ride with ride_cancel_scheduled before ride_schedule; a first ride replaces nothing.
- [MUST IP-12b] An airport pickup is 20 minutes after the flight's scheduled arrival, and a station pickup after a train 20 minutes after the train's arrival (its projected arrival where status_events gives one), unless the customer says otherwise.
- [SHOULD IP-13] The agent should finish with one written reply: what was done, amounts and currency, ids, what is pending and who owns it, and what could not be done and why.

40_coverage_additions.name: 40_coverage_additions
40_coverage_additions.text:
## Coverage additions

- [MUST CV-CANCEL-MONEY] [synthetic] flight_cancel and rail_cancel move no TripDesk money: the agent refunds with issue_refund only the remaining value they return as cash, and never pays cash for a value returned as a credit or voucher, except where the DOT rule gives a cash refund (P-DOT-REFUND, P-DOT-CASH).
- [MUST CV-DB-FARE] [V1] A Deutsche Bahn Flexpreis ticket is refunded free before its first day of validity and for 30 EUR from that day, a Sparpreis ticket is cancelled only before its first day of validity and as a voucher for its price minus 10 EUR, and a Super Sparpreis ticket is never refunded.
- [MUST CV-AMTRAK-CANCEL] [synthetic] When Amtrak cancels a train, the fare is refunded in full and no Value fare forfeit applies.
- [MUST CV-CLAIM] [synthetic] Compensation the law gives against a carrier (P-EU261, P-UK261, P-EU-RAIL) is claimed from that vendor through vendor_send with request_type compensation_claim for the amount compute_entitlement gives (for a flight, the per passenger figure times the booking's pax, in one claim per booking), and TripDesk never pays it from its own money; a rail delay is claimed only once the delayed train has arrived (its projected or actual arrival is before now), so while the passenger is still travelling the agent files nothing and tells the customer the claim follows arrival.
- [MUST CV-BAG-FEE] [V1] A checked bag not delivered within 12 hours of a US domestic arrival (15 or 30 hours on an international itinerary) is significantly delayed, and once the passenger filed a Mishandled Baggage Report the operating carrier refunds the bag fee.
- [MUST CV-BAG-CLAIM] [synthetic] A delayed, lost or damaged bag is claimed from the operating carrier through vendor_send with request_type bag_claim, for the bag fee or the documented cost, and TripDesk never pays a bag claim itself.
- [MUST CV-RIDE-FARE] [synthetic] A disputed ride charge (a fee, toll, tip or cancellation fee) is sent to the ride vendor through vendor_send with request_type fare_review, and TripDesk refunds only the amount the vendor approved.
- [MUST CV-UBER-RESERVE] [V1] An Uber Reserve ride is free to cancel up to 60 minutes before pickup, and inside 60 minutes is charged a cancellation fee only once a driver accepted it; the fee amount is [synthetic].
- [MUST CV-LOST-ITEM] [synthetic] A lost item is reported to the ride vendor through vendor_send with request_type lost_item, and the agent never promises the item's return or pays its value.
- [MUST CV-IR-TDR] [V1] An Indian Railways TDR is filed through vendor_send with request_type tdr_filing, and for a train more than 3 hours (180 minutes, the tdr_late_min in the vendor's fare_rules) late it counts only if filed before the train's actual departure.
- [SHOULD CV-STATUS] The agent should read the delayed flight with flight_get_status before rebooking after an inbound delay, and take the projected arrival from it.
- [MUST CV-CANCEL-STATUS] [synthetic] flight_cancel, rail_cancel and hotel_cancel cancel only a confirmed booking (flight_cancel and rail_cancel only before departure), and ride_cancel_scheduled only a scheduled ride, each only where the message asks for that cancellation (IP-2); the vendor booking and its platform_booking_id row then both take status cancelled, and flight_cancel and rail_cancel record in the booking's details a cancel_event at the current time by the customer.
- [MUST CV-SEATS] [synthetic] A seat count moves only with a booking: flight_cancel and flight_change return the booking's pax to the inventory row (product_id) of each flight the booking leaves, and flight_change takes them from the new flight's row, which must hold at least that many seats.
- [MUST CV-REASON] [synthetic] The reason_code of issue_refund and issue_refund_legacy says why the money is owed: airline_cancelled where the carrier (an airline or a rail operator) cancelled the trip or changed it significantly (P-DOT-REFUND), customer_cancel_free where the customer cancelled within a free cancellation window, or where a hotel property cancelled or failed to provide the stay (a cancel_event by property, or cause supplier_fault) and kept no fee, customer_cancel where the customer cancelled and the fare rule kept a forfeit, or where a prepaid car was not picked up and the vendor kept its no_show_fee (CR-ENT-CANCEL), fare_review_approved where a vendor approved a disputed ride charge (CV-RIDE-FARE), smoking_fee_dispute where a disputed property smoking fee is reversed, and vendor_cancelled where a car vendor or cruise line cancelled or failed to provide the booking, or a cruise line delayed it 3 or more calendar days (CR-CAR-NOCAR, CR-FMC-REFUND).

50_car_rental_and_cruises.name: 50_car_rental_and_cruises
50_car_rental_and_cruises.text:
## 50 Car rental and cruises

Car rental vendors (car_rental) and cruise lines (cruise_line) are read with car_get_reservation and cruise_get_booking.
A car vendor bills its own charges after the rental (rental_charges) to the renter's card; those never pass through
TripDesk.

- [MUST CR-CAR-CANCEL] [synthetic] car_cancel cancels only a confirmed reservation before its pickup_time and only where the message asks for it (IP-2); it moves no TripDesk money, and the vendor booking and its platform_booking_id row then both take status cancelled with a cancel_event by the customer.
- [MUST CR-HERTZ-CANCEL] [V1] A Hertz Pay Now reservation cancelled more than 24 hours before pickup keeps a 50 USD fee and one cancelled within 24 hours a 100 USD fee, and a reservation neither cancelled nor picked up by its pickup_time forfeits the whole prepaid amount: car_cancel applies the cancel terms in the vendor's fare_rules for the reservation's rate_plan, and quote_cancellation keeps that fee from the refundable amount.
- [MUST CR-TURO-CANCEL] [V1] A refundable Turo trip cancelled at least 24 hours before its start is refunded in full; cancelled later, Turo keeps half of one day's average trip price for a trip of two days or shorter and one full day's for a longer trip: car_cancel and quote_cancellation apply the cancel terms in the vendor's fare_rules.
- [MUST CR-TURO-HOST] [V1] Turo is merchant of record for its trips and refunds the guest itself, in full when the host cancels or does not show: TripDesk never pays a Turo trip back with issue_refund (IP-16).
- [MUST CR-CAR-NOCAR] [synthetic] When a car vendor provides no car for a confirmed reservation (vendor status no_car, a cancel_event by the vendor), quote_cancellation keeps no fee, issue_refund pays the prepaid amount back with reason_code vendor_cancelled (CV-REASON), and the extra cost of a replacement rental is asked from the vendor through vendor_send with request_type replacement_claim; the agent never promises that money (IP-8).
- [MUST CR-CAR-FLIGHT] [synthetic] When the flight named on a car reservation will arrive after the reservation's pickup_time, the agent reads the projected_arrival with flight_get_status and moves the pickup with car_change to 60 minutes after that projected arrival, leaving the return_time as booked.
- [MUST CR-CAR-EXTEND] [V1] Changing or extending a rental may raise its charges: car_change charges each added rental day at the reservation's daily_rate to the original payment of a pay_now reservation, and only up to the max_extra the message authorizes (IP-2).
- [MUST CR-TURO-EXTEND] [V1] A Turo trip is extended only by a trip change request made through Turo and accepted by the host: the agent sends it with vendor_send request_type extension_request and never changes a Turo return_time with car_change.
- [MUST CR-CAR-DISPUTE] [synthetic] car_dispute_charge disputes only a billed rental_charges line that the message disputes, and only once.
- [MUST CR-CAR-MONEY] [synthetic] A rental_charges line is billed by the car vendor, so TripDesk never pays one back with issue_refund: a reversed line is reversed by the vendor, and an upheld line is not refunded.
- [MUST CR-CAR-NY] [V1] In New York (state NY on the reservation) a damage claim must be made on return, or within 10 days of an after-hours return_mode, and loss of use and administrative fees are never recovered from the renter: car_dispute_charge reverses a damage line billed later than that and any loss_of_use or admin_fee line.
- [MUST CR-TURO-DAMAGE] [V1] A Turo host must report damage no more than 24 hours after the trip ends: car_dispute_charge reverses a damage line billed later than damage_report_hours after returned_at.
- [MUST CR-CAR-FUEL] [V1] A fuel charge is due only when the car came back with less fuel than it left with: car_dispute_charge reverses a fuel line when fuel_in is at least fuel_out, except a low mileage fuel fee the vendor's terms set (CR-AVIS-FUEL).
- [MUST CR-CAR-LATE] [V1] Hertz charges no late return within a 30 minute grace period and Turo none for 0 to 29 minutes late: car_dispute_charge reverses a late_return line when returned_at is within late_grace_min of return_time, and upholds it when the car came back later (CR-COUNTER-LATE).
- [MUST CR-CAR-INCIDENTAL] [V1] Hertz charges 400 USD for smoking in the car, and Turo 150 USD plus a 3 percent fee for a cleaning or smoking violation: car_dispute_charge upholds a cleaning, smoking or toll line, and the agent never refunds it.
- [SHOULD CR-CAR-DEPOSIT] [V1] A deposit authorization may exceed the estimated charges and the card issuer releases the excess with some delay: the agent should explain the deposit_hold from car_get_reservation and never treats a hold as a charge to refund.
- [MUST CR-CAR-LAW] [V1] No statute gives a renter compensation for a car rental; state law only limits damage claims (CR-CAR-NY), and compute_entitlement gives none on a car booking.
- [MUST CR-CRUISE-CANCEL] [synthetic] cruise_cancel cancels only a confirmed booking before its all_aboard time and only where the message asks for it (IP-2); it moves no TripDesk money, and the vendor booking and its platform_booking_id row then both take status cancelled with a cancel_event by the customer.
- [MUST CR-CCL-CANCEL] [V1] A Carnival cruise of 6 days or longer cancelled by the guest is free up to 91 days before sailing, keeps the deposit from 90 to 56 days, the deposit or 50 percent of the total fare (whichever is greater) from 55 to 30 days, the deposit or 75 percent from 29 to 15 days, and 100 percent at 14 days or less (2 to 5 day cruises are free up to 76 days): cruise_cancel and quote_cancellation apply the cancel_schedule in the vendor's fare_rules by the booking's nights and the days left before all_aboard.
- [MUST CR-RCL-CANCEL] [V1] A Royal Caribbean cruise of 5 to 14 nights booked before 2026-10-11 and cancelled by the guest keeps nothing at 90 days or more before sailing, 25 percent of the fare from 89 to 75 days, 50 percent from 74 to 61, 75 percent from 60 to 31 and 100 percent at 30 days or less, never refunds the deposit, and refunds prepaid taxes and fees (taxes_fees): cruise_cancel and quote_cancellation apply the cancel_schedule in the vendor's fare_rules.
- [MUST CR-FMC-REFUND] [V2] A cruise from a US port that the line cancels, or delays by 3 or more calendar days, is nonperformance and the passenger is owed a refund in money; a future cruise credit or onboard credit replaces it only if the passenger agrees, whatever the line's contract offers: compute_entitlement gives it, and issue_refund pays the refundable amount quote_cancellation gives with reason_code vendor_cancelled.
- [MUST CR-EU-SEA] [V1] The EU sea passenger rules on re-routing, refund and compensation for delay or cancellation do not apply to cruise passengers: compute_entitlement gives no entitlement under them on a cruise.
- [MUST CR-NOSHOW] [V1] A guest who does not board at embarkation gets no refund, and rejoining the ship is at the guest's own cost: quote_cancellation gives nothing refundable on a cruise that sailed or whose status is missed_embarkation, and the agent never refunds it.
- [MUST CR-FLIGHT-PORT] [synthetic] When a flight to the embarkation port will arrive less than 180 minutes before the cruise's all_aboard time, the agent rebooks with flight_change, before the booked flight departs, the earliest flight that departs at or after the booked flight's original departure and arrives at least 180 minutes before all_aboard.
- [MUST CR-ITIN] [V1] A cruise line may change the itinerary, ports and times without liability: when an itinerary_change moves the disembarkation, the agent moves a flight home that departs less than 180 minutes [synthetic] after the new disembark time with flight_change to the earliest flight departing at least 180 minutes after it, the cost charged to the customer only within the amount the message authorizes (IP-2), and asks the line for no compensation.
- [MUST CR-OBC] [synthetic] Onboard credit has no cash value: no refund pays an onboard_credit, and issue_refund never exceeds the refundable amount quote_cancellation gives, which excludes it.
- [SHOULD CR-FINAL-PAY] [V1] A cruise line may cancel a booking whose final payment is late: the agent should give the customer the final_payment_due date from cruise_get_booking.

60_disputes_care.name: 60_disputes_care
60_disputes_care.text:
## 60 Card disputes, EU261 care and travel insurance

Background: a chargeback is a card dispute the cardholder files with the card issuer against a charge TripDesk
took as merchant of record; the card network (Visa, Mastercard) decides it. A travel insurance policy sold with a
booking is a contract between the customer and the insurer, and TripDesk is not the insurer.

- [MUST CB-OPEN] [V1] While a chargeback get_chargebacks lists is open (the payment's dispute_status open), the card network decides the money: a cardholder is never credited twice through both a dispute and a credit, so the agent never refunds that booking with issue_refund or issue_refund_legacy (issue_refund already refuses it) and answers the dispute only with respond_chargeback, once.
- [MUST CB-CLOSED] [V1] An accepted, won or lost chargeback closes the money question for its payment: issue_refund refuses a payment whose dispute_status is won or lost, and the agent never refunds the booking outside the network's decision; a chargeback still open on the same payment is answered once with respond_chargeback (CB-OPEN), and answering it pays nothing.
- [MUST CB-WINDOW] [V1] respond_chargeback answers a chargeback only before its respond_by, set from the network's response_days (30 calendar days for Visa [V1], 45 for Mastercard [V2]); after it the dispute stays with the cardholder and the agent records the missed window with add_note.
- [MUST CB-VENDOR-FAULT] [synthetic] Where the vendor failed to deliver the booking (a cancel_event by airline, vendor or property whatever its cause, weather included, or cause supplier_fault), the agent accepts the chargeback with respond_chargeback decision accept and never contests it; it contests only where the customer owes the amount under the fare_rules or property_policy (the service was delivered, or the customer cancelled late or did not show).
- [MUST CB-EVIDENCE] [synthetic] A respond_chargeback contest carries evidence read from the booking: the vendor booking status (flown, no_show, completed), the fare class and its fare_rules or the property_policy, and the cancel_event.
- [MUST CB-RECOVER] [synthetic] A chargeback accepted for a vendor's fault (CB-VENDOR-FAULT), by the agent with respond_chargeback or before, is a supplier loss: the agent records it with reclassify_cancellation cause supplier_fault and claims exactly the chargeback amount from that vendor in one vendor_send with request_type chargeback_recovery (IP-3); an open chargeback is not yet a loss, and other requests to the vendor (compensation, care, bag or information) are not recovery claims and follow their own rules.
- [SHOULD CB-FCBA] [V1] A customer who asks how to dispute a charge should be told that the billing error notice must reach the card issuer within 60 days after the first statement that shows the charge, and that Visa lets the issuer file a dispute within 120 calendar days.
- [MUST CARE-DUE] [V1] On a cancelled EU flight, or one whose departure is delayed 2 hours or more (1500 km or less), 3 hours or more (intra-EU over 1500 km, other flights of 1500 to 3500 km) or 4 hours or more (all others), the operating carrier owes meals and refreshments in reasonable relation to the waiting time and two calls or e-mails, and hotel accommodation with transport between airport and hotel when the new departure is at least the day after: compute_care gives these items_due from the departure_delay_min, distance_km, intra_eu, cancel_event and reroute.
- [MUST CARE-EXTRAORDINARY] [V1] Care is owed even when the cause was extraordinary and compute_entitlement gives no compensation; a carrier's refusal of a care_expense_claim is escalated with escalate to supplier_relations with the claimed amount, and TripDesk never pays a care cost itself.
- [MUST CARE-CLAIM] [V1] Where the carrier did not give care, the customer's receipts for it are claimed from the operating carrier through vendor_send with request_type care_expense_claim, for the claimable amount compute_care gives, in the currency it gives; an item the carrier gave in kind (care_provided) or a purchase that is not care is never claimed, and a care claim is never added into a compensation_claim.
- [SHOULD CARE-CHOICE] [V1] On a cancellation or a departure delay of 5 hours or more (reroute_or_refund from compute_care), the agent should tell the customer of the choice between a refund of the ticket within seven days, re-routing at the earliest opportunity and re-routing at a later date.
- [MUST INS-INSURER] [V1] The insurer of a policy (insurer_id in insurance_policies) is never TripDesk: a premium is refunded only by insurance_cancel and a claim is paid only by the insurer through insurance_file_claim, and the agent never pays a premium or a claim with issue_refund or issue_refund_legacy.
- [MUST INS-FREELOOK] [V1] Inside the plan's free look (15 days after purchase, the free_look_days in the insurer's fare_rules, before the trip starts and with no claim filed) insurance_cancel refunds the whole premium; after it the premium is kept, so the agent runs insurance_cancel after the free look only where the message accepts losing the premium (IP-2).
- [MUST INS-REFUNDS-FIRST] [V1] A claim is for the loss no one else pays: before insurance_file_claim the agent takes what law or the vendor owes (compute_entitlement, quote_cancellation, issue_refund) and claims for a booking only its paid amount less the refundable amount quote_cancellation gives, the refunds already paid and any value the vendor returned as a credit (an eCredit, voucher or future flight credit counts as recovered), so a booking cancelled for a credit leaves nothing to claim; insurance_file_claim never pays a credited value.
- [MUST INS-NO-DOUBLE] [synthetic] The agent never files insurance_file_claim for a booking whose payment has an open, won or lost chargeback (dispute_status), since the card network already decides that money.
- [MUST INS-REASON] [V1] The reason of insurance_file_claim is the cause the booking shows: carrier_disruption_weather when the carrier cancelled for weather, carrier_disruption_mechanical when it cancelled for a mechanical failure (covered by Travel Guard only), strike, sickness_or_injury, trip_delay when the carrier delayed the trip without cancelling it, cancel_for_any_reason only on a policy with cfar true, and change_of_mind, which neither plan covers.
- [MUST INS-DELAY] [V1] Trip delay pays only once the delay reaches the plan's trip_delay_min_hours, and at most the plan's trip_delay_daily_max per traveller for each started day of delay: insurance_file_claim caps a trip_delay claim at that.
- [SHOULD INS-UNCOVERED] Before filing a reason the plan's covered_reasons do not list, the agent should tell the customer the insurer will deny it, and should file it only where the message asks for the claim anyway.
- [MUST INS-WINDOW] [V1] insurance_file_claim files a claim with the insurer, never with TripDesk, within 90 days after the loss (the claim_days_after_loss in the insurer's fare_rules, counted from the policy's trip_end).

70_rerouting_rail.name: 70_rerouting_rail
70_rerouting_rail.text:
## 70 Re-routing, rail changes and journey scope

- [MUST GP-CARE-DENIED] [V1] A passenger denied boarding against their will is owed care and the choice of re-routing or refund at once, with or without a recorded delay (EU261 Art 4(3): "the operating air carrier shall immediately compensate them in accordance with Article 7 and assist them in accordance with Articles 8 and 9"): compute_care gives the items_due for a booking whose data has denied_boarding, with hotel and transport when the reroute departs on a later day.
- [MUST GP-JOURNEY] [V2] The flights of one through ticket (ticket_group) are one journey (CJEU C-537/17 Wegener: "those flights constitute a whole for the purposes of the right to compensation"): compute_entitlement and compute_care judge every leg by the region of the journey's first flight, never by the leg's own region.
- [MUST GP-REROUTE] [V1] When the airline cancelled the flight (a cancel_event by airline), denied boarding or caused a missed connection (missed_connection), a passenger who does not take the refund is re-routed at no cost with flight_reroute: on the airline's own flight, or on another airline (new_vendor_id) only where EU261 or UK261 applies (Art 8(1)(b): "re-routing, under comparable transport conditions, to their final destination at the earliest opportunity") or the airline's fare_rules give reroute_other_carrier, every condition it lists (when) holds and new_vendor_id is one of its partners, and only when the airline has no flight of its own on the route arriving as early. Delta's contract leaves another carrier to "Delta's sole discretion" (Rule 19.A), so it gives no such right.
- [SHOULD GP-REROUTE-EARLIEST] The agent should re-route on the earliest arriving flight flight_search returns, narrowed with arrive_by to the time the customer must arrive, and record a refused request for another airline with add_note.
- [MUST GP-RAIL-CHANGE] [V1] rail_change moves a confirmed Deutsche Bahn reservation before departure to a later train on the same route by the fare rule in the vendor's fare_rules: a Flexpreis changes free until the day before its first day of validity and for 30 EUR from that day, a Sparpreis for 10 EUR [V2] only before its first day of validity, and a Super Sparpreis never; the change fee plus the fare_difference is charged to the original payment only within the max_fare_difference the message authorizes (IP-2).
- [MUST GP-AMTRAK-CHANGE] [V1] rail_change moves a confirmed Amtrak Flex reservation before departure to a later train on the same route with "No fee, difference in fare may apply", the fare_difference charged only within the max_fare_difference the message authorizes (IP-2), and never changes an Amtrak Value fare ("Changes are not permitted").
- [MUST GP-RAIL-REROUTE] [V1] When the operator cancelled the train (a cancel_event by vendor) or its own late train made the passenger miss the reserved one (missed_connection), the operator rebooks the passenger on its next available train (Amtrak: "Every reasonable effort will be made to rebook you on the next available service"; EU rail: Regulation 2021/782 Art 18 [V2]) at no cost [synthetic]: rail_change makes that change free, also after the booked departure, and the agent takes the earliest train rail_search returns.
- [MUST GP-RAIL-EXCHANGE] [synthetic] A passenger who accepted the operator's move to another train after a cancellation (exchanged_from on the reservation, exchange_accepted true) holds the new ticket: its own fare rules decide a later cancellation (CV-DB-FARE, CV-CANCEL-MONEY), and the cancelled train gives no refund right on it.
- [MUST GP-LH-LIGHT] [V2] A Lufthansa Light fare is kept in full on a voluntary cancellation and its unused taxes are refunded (General Conditions of Carriage Art 10.3.1 [V1]: "an amount equal to the fare paid, less any reasonable service charges or cancellation fees"): flight_cancel and quote_cancellation keep the booking's total less its taxes and return the taxes as cash.
- [MUST GP-FR-REGULAR] [V2] A Ryanair Regular fare is non-refundable (terms 10.1: "all amounts you pay for flights operated by us (including amounts for optional services) are non-refundable"), and a passenger who does not travel gets the government taxes back less the tax refund administration fee (terms 4.2), 20 EUR [V2]: flight_cancel and quote_cancellation keep the total less the taxes plus the tax_refund_fee in the vendor's fare_rules, and return the rest as cash.
- [MUST GP-NO-TERMS] [synthetic] A write tool changes nothing and answers with an error when the booking lacks the terms or times it applies (hotel_cancel without a property_policy, flight_cancel without cancel terms for the fare, cruise_cancel without a cancel_schedule band, rail_change for a fare with no change_fee): the agent never guesses the terms, and asks the vendor with vendor_send only where it still needs them (a refund the law gives, such as P-DOT-REFUND, needs no fare terms).
- [MUST GP-VENDOR-REPLY] [synthetic] A vendor answers vendor_send from its own records of the booking: KU's refund_status reply names the refund it paid on that booking or says none was paid, and River North answers a fee_waiver by its terms (SC-RIVERNORTH) and refuses it, so the agent tells the customer the fee stands.

71_counter_car_rental.name: 71_counter_car_rental
71_counter_car_rental.text:
## 71 Counter car rental: Sixt, Avis and Budget, Enterprise

Sixt, Avis (Budget runs on the same terms) and Enterprise are counter car rental vendors (car_rental), read with
car_get_reservation like Hertz. Each sets its own cancel terms per rate_plan, late return grace, fuel and damage
rules in its fare_rules. Turo stays the only peer to peer vendor (CR-TURO-HOST).

- [MUST CR-SIXT-CANCEL] [V2] A Sixt prepaid reservation cancelled 24 hours or more before pickup keeps a 100 USD fee and one cancelled less than 24 hours before pickup a 200 USD fee, and a prepaid reservation not picked up is not refunded: car_cancel and quote_cancellation apply the pay_now terms in the vendor's fare_rules.
- [MUST CR-AVIS-CANCEL] [V1] An Avis or Budget Pay Now reservation cancelled more than 24 hours before pick-up keeps a 50 USD fee and one cancelled within 24 hours a 150 USD fee, and a no-show refunds no portion of the prepaid amount: car_cancel and quote_cancellation apply the pay_now terms.
- [MUST CR-AVIS-PAYLATER] [V1] An Avis Pay Later reservation not cancelled at least 24 hours before pick-up carries a 75 USD fee that Avis bills to the card on file, and none when the flight on the reservation was cancelled: car_cancel records a billed fee as a rental_charges line (kind cancel_fee) and waives it when status_events shows that flight cancelled; TripDesk refunds nothing for it (CR-CAR-MONEY).
- [MUST CR-ENT-CANCEL] [V1] An Enterprise prepaid reservation cancelled more than 24 hours before pickup keeps a 50 USD fee and one cancelled less than 24 hours before a 100 USD fee, and a no-show is refunded less a 100 USD no-show fee: car_cancel and quote_cancellation apply the pay_now terms and their no_show_fee.
- [MUST CR-COUNTER-LATE] [V1] Enterprise charges no late return for 29 minutes, Sixt bills its 20 USD late fee from two hours after the due time, and Avis publishes no grace: car_dispute_charge reverses a late_return line only when returned_at is within the vendor's late_grace_min of return_time.
- [MUST CR-AVIS-FUEL] [V1] Avis bills a flat fuel fee on a car driven less than 75 miles unless the renter shows a fuel receipt, even when the gauge reads full: car_dispute_charge upholds that fuel line when miles_driven is under low_mileage_fuel_fee_miles and fuel_receipt is false.
- [MUST CR-PICKUP-DAMAGE] [V1] Damage recorded at pickup is not the renter's: car_dispute_charge reverses a damage line, and the loss_of_use, admin_fee, diminished_value and appraisal_fee lines billed with it, when the damage_area is in the reservation's pickup_damage.
- [MUST CR-COUNTER-INCIDENTAL] [V1] Sixt charges cleaning or smoking up to 400 USD and Avis smoking up to 450 USD: car_dispute_charge upholds a cleaning or smoking line, and the agent never refunds it.
- [SHOULD CR-COUNTER-DEPOSIT] [V1] Sixt may hold up to three times the estimated charges and at least 200 USD, Avis the estimated charges plus a deposit, and Enterprise releases its authorization at return: the agent should explain the deposit_hold from car_get_reservation and never treats a hold as a charge to refund.
- [MUST CR-COUNTER-PEER] [synthetic] A Sixt, Avis or Enterprise reservation is changed with car_change like Hertz (CR-CAR-FLIGHT, CR-CAR-EXTEND); the Turo rules (CR-TURO-HOST, CR-TURO-EXTEND, CR-TURO-DAMAGE) never apply to them.

72_card_trip_protection.name: 72_card_trip_protection
72_card_trip_protection.text:
## 72 Card trip protection: American Express and Chase Sapphire Reserve

Background: trip protection on a credit card is insurance the card's benefit administrator (vendors of type
card_benefit) pays to the cardholder. card_benefit_get lists a customer's card_benefits and their claims;
card_benefit_file_claim files one. TripDesk is not the insurer and pays no part of a claim.

- [MUST TP-PAID-WITH] [V1] A card benefit covers only a trip paid with that card: American Express needs the full amount charged to the Eligible Card (points allowed), Chase all or a portion charged to the Covered Card or paid with its rewards; card_benefit_file_claim refuses a booking whose payment card_last4 is not the benefit's card, and a benefit whose status is not active.
- [MUST TP-EXCESS] [V1] Both programs pay in excess of what the vendor and the law pay: before card_benefit_file_claim the agent takes the refund quote_cancellation gives and issue_refund pays, and claims only what is left; a cancellation kept as a vendor credit leaves nothing to claim.
- [MUST TP-NO-DOUBLE] [synthetic] A payment with an open, won or lost chargeback (dispute_status) is decided by the card network: card_benefit_file_claim refuses it, and the agent never claims the same booking and coverage twice.
- [MUST TP-REASON] [V1] The reason of card_benefit_file_claim is the cause the booking shows; American Express trip cancellation does not cover a strike, Chase does, and neither covers a change_of_plans; a supplier's insolvency is not covered by Chase and goes to the card issuer as a dispute.
- [MUST TP-DELAY] [V1] Trip delay pays after more than 6 hours of delay (Chase also for an overnight stay), up to 500 USD per trip (per traveler for Chase), for the covered causes; American Express pays at most 2 delay claims per card in 12 months and covers round trips only: card_benefit_file_claim decides it from the flight's delay and the program's terms.
- [MUST TP-CAPS] [V1] Trip cancellation and interruption pay at most 10,000 USD per trip (per traveler for Chase, 20,000 USD per trip) and never more than the booking's cost less refunds and vendor credits: card_benefit_file_claim pays at most that.
- [MUST TP-NOTICE] [V1] American Express takes notice within 60 days of the loss; Chase within 20 days for trip cancellation or interruption and 60 days for trip delay: card_benefit_file_claim refuses a claim later than the program's report_within_days.
- [SHOULD TP-DOCS] [V1] The agent should tell the cardholder which documents the program asks for (the documents in the program's terms) and its proof deadline (proof_days).
- [MUST TP-NOT-TRIPDESK] [synthetic] The agent never pays a card benefit claim or its denied amount with issue_refund or issue_refund_legacy, and never promises a claim outcome before card_benefit_file_claim gives it.

73_msc_ncl.name: 73_msc_ncl
73_msc_ncl.text:
## 73 Cruise lines: MSC and Norwegian

MSC Cruises and Norwegian Cruise Line are cruise lines (cruise_line) read with cruise_get_booking. Each sets its
own cancel_schedule, final payment date and future cruise credit terms in its fare_rules.

- [MUST CR-NCL-CANCEL] [V1] A Norwegian cruise in a Club Balcony Suite or lower category cancelled by the guest keeps 25 percent of the fare from 119 to 91 days before sailing, 50 percent from 90 to 61, 75 percent from 60 to 31 and 100 percent at 30 days or less; a Haven, Suite or Garden Villa keeps 25 percent from 119 to 106 days, 50 percent from 105 to 91, 75 percent from 90 to 61 and 100 percent at 60 days or less: cruise_cancel and quote_cancellation apply the cancel_schedule by the booking's cabin_category.
- [MUST CR-MSC-CANCEL] [V2] An MSC cruise cancelled by the guest keeps 15 percent of the total fare at 60 days or more before sailing, 75 percent from 59 to 10 days and 100 percent from 9 to 0 days, assessed on the fare excluding taxes, which come back: cruise_cancel and quote_cancellation apply the cancel_schedule in the vendor's fare_rules.
- [SHOULD CR-CRUISE-FINAL-DAYS] [V1] Norwegian takes final payment 120 days before sailing, and MSC 75 days before a cruise of 4 nights or less and 90 days before one of 5 to 14 nights [V2]; a booking unpaid by then may be cancelled with charges: the agent should give the final_payment_due from cruise_get_booking.
- [MUST CR-FCC] [V1] A future cruise credit offered when the line cancels or fails to perform is an alternative the guest may decline: the agent offers the refund in money first (CR-FMC-REFUND), paid with issue_refund, and never accepts the line_offer cruise_get_booking shows without the message saying so.
- [MUST CR-NCL-NOSHOW] [V1] Norwegian refunds nothing to a guest who does not board, and treats a name or date change as a cancellation: quote_cancellation gives nothing refundable on a sailed or missed embarkation (CR-NOSHOW).
- [SHOULD CR-MSC-NAME] [V2] MSC charges a 50 USD name change fee: the agent should say so before asking the line to change a guest's name.

74_us_carriers_eurostar.name: 74_us_carriers_eurostar
74_us_carriers_eurostar.text:
## 74 United, American, easyJet and Eurostar

Background: United Airlines (V-UA) and American Airlines (V-AA) are US carriers under DOT rules, easyJet (V-U2)
flies under UK261 and EU261, and Eurostar (V-EUROSTAR) runs cross-border trains between London, Paris, Brussels
and Amsterdam. Each sells under its own contract of carriage, and the fare rules below come from each brand's own
pages. A care cost claimed under a US carrier's customer service plan is the carrier's promise, not a statute.

- [MUST WC-US-24H] [V1] A US airline lets a ticket bought 7 or more days before departure be cancelled without penalty for 24 hours after purchase: flight_cancel inside the free_cancel_hours in the vendor's fare_rules after the booking's created_at, with at least free_cancel_min_days left before departure, returns the whole fare as cash, and issue_refund pays it with reason_code customer_cancel_free.
- [MUST WC-DOT-ACCEPTED] [V1] The DOT cash refund for a cancelled flight is owed only where the passenger did not accept the alternative: a re-routing the passenger accepted (reroute accepted on the vendor booking) leaves no refund, and compute_entitlement gives none.
- [MUST WC-UA-BASIC] [V2] A United Basic Economy ticket cannot be changed, and once the 24-hour window has passed it keeps no value when cancelled: flight_change refuses it (changeable false in the vendor's fare_rules), flight_cancel refuses it (cancellable false), and the agent never refunds or credits it.
- [MUST WC-UA-ECONOMY] [V2] A United Economy ticket from the US has no change fee and no cancellation fee, any fare difference applies, and a voluntary cancellation returns its value as a future flight credit, never cash: flight_cancel returns refund_form future_flight_credit, and issue_refund never pays it.
- [MUST WC-AA-BASIC] [V2] An American Basic Economy ticket cannot be changed, and after the 24-hour window only an AAdvantage member (the customer's loyalty_program) may cancel it, for a Trip Credit of the fare less a 99 USD fee within the 48 contiguous states: flight_cancel applies the cancel_fee and loyalty_program in the vendor's fare_rules, returns no value to anyone else, and issue_refund never pays the credit.
- [MUST WC-AA-MAIN] [V2] An American Main Cabin ticket from North or South America has no change fee, any fare difference applies, and a voluntary cancellation returns its value as a Trip Credit valid for one year, never cash: flight_cancel returns refund_form trip_credit, and issue_refund never pays it.
- [MUST WC-US-PLAN] [V2] United and American commit in their customer service plans, for a cancellation or delay in their control (controllable on the vendor booking), to a meal once the passenger waits 3 hours or more and to a hotel with ground transport for an overnight wait, and United pays back at most 200 USD a night for a hotel it could not provide: compute_care gives these items_due under regime carrier_plan, the receipts are claimed from the carrier through vendor_send with request_type care_expense_claim for the claimable amount, and TripDesk never pays them.
- [MUST WC-US-NOCOMP] [V2] Outside its control (weather, air traffic control) a US carrier commits to no care, and no US carrier owes cash compensation for a delay (P-DOT-NODELAY): the agent never sends a compensation_claim to V-UA or V-AA through vendor_send, and never claims a cost the plan does not list (a lounge pass, a lost deposit).
- [MUST P-UK261] [V1] UK261 covers passengers departing a UK airport, and those flying to the UK on a UK or EU carrier; for a cancellation or denied boarding the operating carrier owes 220 GBP for flights of 1500 km or less, 350 GBP for 1500 to 3500 km and 520 GBP for all others, per passenger (compute_entitlement gives it times the booking's pax), on the notice, delay and extraordinary circumstances terms of P-EU261, P-EU261-NOTICE and P-EU261-CASELAW: compute_entitlement gives it for region UK, and it is claimed through vendor_send with request_type compensation_claim (CV-CLAIM).
- [MUST P-UK261-CARE] [V1] UK261 Article 9 care is owed on a UK flight as CARE-DUE gives it on an EU flight, and claimed in GBP: compute_care gives it under regime uk261_care.
- [MUST WC-U2-CHANGE] [V2] An easyJet flight can be changed up to 2 hours before departure, for a change fee per passenger per flight (30 GBP more than 60 days out, the change_fee in the vendor's fare_rules) plus any higher fare, and a lower fare is not refunded: flight_change charges change_fee times pax plus the fare_difference, only within the amount the message authorizes (IP-2).
- [MUST WC-U2-CANCEL] [V2] easyJet refunds a booking cancelled within a day of making it less a cancellation fee (30 GBP [synthetic], the free_cancel_fee in the vendor's fare_rules) and gives no refund after that: flight_cancel returns no value outside the window, and issue_refund pays only the refundable amount quote_cancellation gives.
- [MUST WC-ES-EXCHANGE] [V1] A Eurostar Standard or Plus ticket is exchanged with no fee up to 1 hour before departure and a Premier ticket up to 2 days after departure, with any fare difference payable: rail_change moves the reservation to a later train rail_search lists on the same route, by the change_until_min and change_fee in the vendor's fare_rules, charges the fare_difference to the original payment only within the amount the message authorizes (IP-2), and refunds nothing for a cheaper train (no_lower_fare_refund) [synthetic].
- [MUST WC-ES-REFUND] [V1] A Eurostar Standard or Plus ticket is refunded up to 7 days before departure less 25 GBP or EUR per leg per person, a Premier ticket with no fee up to 48 hours after its departure, and a SNAP ticket never: rail_cancel applies the cancel_until_min and cancel_fee per pax in the vendor's fare_rules, and issue_refund pays only the refundable amount quote_cancellation gives.
- [MUST WC-ES-CANCELLED] [V1] When Eurostar cancels a train and the arrival would be 60 minutes or more late, the passenger may take a full refund, or a later train as GP-RAIL-REROUTE gives: quote_cancellation keeps nothing on a booking whose cancel_event is by the vendor, and issue_refund pays it with reason_code airline_cancelled.
- [MUST WC-ES-DELAY] [V1] Eurostar pays a delay of 60 to 119 minutes with 25 percent of the affected leg in cash or a 30 percent e-voucher, and from 120 minutes 50 percent in cash or a 60 percent e-voucher (75 percent from 180 minutes), claimed within three months: the cash figure is the amount compute_entitlement gives (P-EU-RAIL), claimed through vendor_send with request_type compensation_claim, and the agent asks for an e-voucher only where the message chooses it.
- [MUST WC-ES-CARE] [V1] When a Eurostar journey cannot continue on the day, Eurostar reimburses reasonable overnight accommodation, food, transport between station and accommodation and calls, claimed within three months: the receipts are sent through vendor_send with request_type care_expense_claim, and TripDesk never pays them.
- [MUST WC-U2-REROUTE] [V2] When easyJet cancels a flight under EU261 or UK261 it offers "a transfer to an alternative flight" or a refund, and under EU261 or UK261 Art 8(1)(b) the re-routing may be on another airline when easyJet has no flight arriving as early: flight_reroute moves the booking at no cost as GP-REROUTE gives.
- [MUST WC-AA-REROUTE] [V2] American rebooks a passenger whose flight it cancelled "on the next American Airlines flight with available seats at no additional cost", and on "one of our partner airlines" only "If no American flights are available until the next day, and the disruption is caused by us": its fare_rules carry reroute_other_carrier with those two conditions (controllable, no_own_flight_until_next_day) and its partners (British Airways), so flight_reroute moves the booking to a partner only when both hold, else only to an American flight, and the agent never re-routes it on an airline that is not its partner.
